STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.claim: Another theme is the terrible nature of divine chastisement in this world and the next.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.anchor: whether in this world or in the next (vv. 16–17,29–31, 42–44, 48–50)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sūrah's concluding section, verses 42–52, is filled with warnings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This concluding section of the sūrah is replete with warnings.

SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa makes يوم يأتيهم the second object of أنذر, glossing warn them of the punishment of a day; al-Samin objects that this makes the wording redundant. It cannot be a time adverb because no warning occurs that day, whether Judgment, destruction, or the angels’ meeting.
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يوم يأتيهم }: مفعول ثان ل " أنذر " ، أي: خوفهم عذاب يوم، كذا قدره أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r2.claim: نجب is the response to the imperative.

SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari understands omitted القول: wrongdoers either say this arrogantly or express it through conduct, building strongly and hoping for a distant future.
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " على إرادة القول، وفيه وجهان: أن يقولوا ذلك بطرا وأشرا

SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r4.claim: The Sheikh says the omitted speech is from God or the angels addressing them; al-Samin prefers this external speaker over the wrongdoers speaking themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r4.anchor: وهو عندي أظهر من الأول، أعني جريان القول من غيرهم لا منهم.

SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r5.claim: ما لكم answers the oath and uses second person to match أقسمتم; if the oath-takers spoke, they would say ما لنا.
SAMIN-DURR:14:44/r5.anchor: و " مالكم " جواب القسم، وإنما جاء بلفظ الخطاب، لقوله: " أقسمتم " ولو جاء بلفظ المقسمين

ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r1.claim: People are to be warned of the day punishment befalls them, when wrongdoers will beg for a short delay so they can answer God's call and follow the apostles.
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r1.anchor: warn men of the Day when this suffe ring may befall them

ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r2.claim: God answers that they had earlier sworn no resurrection and retribution awaited them; the next verse recalls lessons from prior sinful peoples and parables already given.
ASAD-NOTES:14:44/r2.anchor: were you not aforetime wont to swear that no kind of resurrection and retribution awaited you?

ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n57/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n57/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n57/r1.claim: Asad points to 6:27 as a parallel for the wrongdoers' plea to return and respond to God's call.

ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n58/r1.claim: The literal image is no “going down” or removal: no passage from earthly life to the hereafter and its retribution, reflecting the Qur'anic rejection of afterlife and final judgment by many.
ASAD-NOTES:14:44#n58/r1.anchor: Lit., "that there would be no going down [or "no removal"] whatever for you"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r2.claim: The warning in 14:44 addresses all people; when punishment comes, the wrongdoers ask for a short reprieve so they can answer the call and follow the messengers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r2.anchor: وَأَنذِرِ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ الْعَذَابُ فَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ رَبَّنَا أَخِّرْنَا إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The closing verses 42–52 assure the Prophet and threaten the disbelievers, completing the sūrah's discourse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: These are the concluding verses of the sūrah in which the Prophet (sws) is assured and the disbelievers are threatened.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: If the people will not heed the Prophet, he should leave them to themselves; the verse then indicates what he should do.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if these people do not listen to the Prophet (sws), he should let them be.

IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r1.speaker: كنانة بن عبد ياليل بن عمرو بن عمير
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r1.claim: Kināna answers Kaʿb that his people will not abandon their settled home: their ancestors held its gardens and vineyards, and they have endured challenges there for generations.
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r1.anchor: فأجابه كنانة بن عبد ياليل بن عمرو بن عمير، فقال: من كان يبغينا يريد قتالنا

IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r2.speaker: كنانة بن عبد ياليل بن عمرو بن عمير
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r2.claim: Kināna boasts of inherited armor and sharp swords, saying his people will stand firm and make the stubborn yield to manifest truth.
IBNHISHAM:v2p481/r2.anchor: نقومها حتى يلين شريسها ... ويعرف للحق المبين ظلومها علينا دلاص من تراث محرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r14.claim: The address is to the Prophet; يوم is a second object of أنذر, not an adverb of time, since the Day itself is not when the warning is delivered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r14.anchor: هذا خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم. ويوم منصوب على أنه مفعول ثان لا نذر، ولا يصح أن يكون ظرفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r15.claim: The day is the Resurrection, and the warning targets wrongdoers as the believers receive glad tidings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r15.anchor: وهذا اليوم هو يوم القيامة والمعنى: وأنذر الناس الظالمين، ويبين ذلك قوله: فيقول الذين ظلموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r16.claim: Another view takes the day as their destruction by immediate punishment or their death amid agony and an encounter with angels without glad tidings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r16.anchor: وقيل: اليوم يوم هلاكهم بالعذاب العاجل، أو يوم موتهم معذبين بشدة السكرات، ولقاء الملائكة بلا بشرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r17.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak says their request for delay means asking to be returned to worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r17.anchor: ومعنى التأخر إلى أجل قريب الرد إلى الدنيا قاله الضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r18.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r18.claim: Al-Suddi explains it as asking for respite until a short, fixed term, so they can make up their failure to answer God’s call and follow the messengers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r18.anchor: إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب قاله السدي، أي: لتدارك ما فرطوا من إجابة الدعوة، واتباع الرسل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r19.claim: The phrase implies “it will be said to them,” probably by the angels or by God, as a reproach recalling their denial of resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r19.anchor: أو لم تكونوا هو على إضمار القول والظاهر أن التقدير فيقال لهم، والقائل الملائكة، أو القائل الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r20.claim: Their prior oath was that they would not depart from the earth after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p451/r20.anchor: ومعنى ما لكم من زوال، من الأرض بعد الموت أي:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the words are addressed to the wrongdoers while they are in Hell; the reply is a rebuke and reprimand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: إن هذا القول يكون منهم وهم في النار، ويرد عليهم: أو لم تكونوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers two ways to understand their oath: an arrogant spoken claim, or a claim implicit in their building strongly and hoping for a long future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري أو لم تكونوا أقسمتم على إرادة القول، وفيه وجهان: أن يقولوا ذلك بطرا وأشرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the oath’s answer means they claimed they would remain in the world without death or annihilation, or would not move to another abode; Abu Hayyan objects that they accepted death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزولون بالموت والفناء، وقيل: لا تنتقلون إلى دار أخرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects construing the rebuke as words spoken by the wrongdoers; the apparent sense is that God or angels say it to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r4.anchor: فجعل الزمخشري أو لم تكونوا محكيا بقولهم، وهو مخالف لما قد بيناه من أنه يقال لهم ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p452/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan says “you do not depart by death” is unsound because the wrongdoers admit death; he attributes that view to Mujahid.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r1.claim: The apparent referent of ‘people’ is the disbelievers called wrongdoers, since the verse says punishment will come to them; Abū Ḥayyān and others hold this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r1.anchor: فالمراد بالناس الكفار المعبر عنهم بالظالمين كما يقتضيه ظاهر إتيان العذاب وإلى ذلك ذهب أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r2.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r2.claim: The shift from an implicit reference to naming people as people frames warning as compassionate restraint from wrongdoing, not frightening them merely to distress or harm them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r2.anchor: نكتة العدول اليه من الاضمار على ماقاله شيخ الاسلام الاشعار بأن المراد بالانذار هو الزجر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r3.speaker: الجبائي وأبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r3.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and Abū Muslim understand ‘people’ to include wrongdoers and other morally responsible people: warning applies to both, though punishment particularly overtakes disbelievers; compare 36:11.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r3.anchor: وقال الجبائي : وأبو مسلم : المراد بالناس مايشمل أولئك الظالمين وغيرهم من المكلفين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r4.claim: Yawm yaʾtīhim al-ʿadhāb is the second object of andhir, meaning warn them of its horrors and events; reading it as a temporal adverb fails because the warning is in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r4.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( ( يوم يأتيهم العذاب ( مفعوله الثاني على معنى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r5.claim: The day is the familiar Day of Resurrection, described elsewhere as a day that overwhelms minds.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r5.anchor: والمراد بهذا اليوم اليوم المعهود وهو اليوم الذي وصف بما يذهل الألباب وهو يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r6.claim: Abū Muslim is reported to identify the day as death, when they are tormented by death throes and meet angels without glad tidings, or the day of their destruction by immediate punishment; the latter is challenged as inconsistent with the preceding restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : هو يوم موتهم معذبين بالسكرات ولقاء الملائكة عليهم السلام بلا بشرى وروى ذلك عن أبي مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r7.claim: Calling them ‘those who did wrong’ registers their guilt and explains their distress; the general wording also suggests that wrongdoing at all can lead to this end, without requiring persistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r7.anchor: والعدول عنه إلى مافي النظم الجليل للتسجيل عليهم بالظلم والاشعار بعليته لما ينالهم من الشدة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r8.speaker: الجبائي وأبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r8.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and Abū Muslim take those who did wrong to mean the disbelievers among the people warned.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r8.anchor: والمعنى على ماقال الجبائي وأبو مسلم الذين ظلموا منهم وهم الكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r9.claim: Another view includes everyone among the warned and earlier nations who wronged themselves through idolatry and denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : يقول كل من ظلم بالشرك والتكذيب من المنذرين وغيرهم من الأمم الخالية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r10.claim: Akhkhirnā can mean delay us from punishment, or delay our punishment, with an omitted noun or figurative attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r10.anchor: أي عن العذاب أو أخر عذابنا ففي الكلام تقدير مضاف أو تجوز في النسبة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid say they ask to be returned to worldly life and given respite.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r11.anchor: قال الضحاك ومجاهد : انهم طلبوا الرد إلى الدنيا والامهال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r12.claim: Another explanation is that they ask for punishment to be lifted and to return briefly to a state of moral responsibility so they can do what pleases God.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : إنهم طلبوا رفع العذاب والرجوع إلى حال التكليف مدة يسيرة يعملون فيها ما يرضيه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r13.claim: In the interpretation attributed to Abū Muslim, they ask that their lifespans be delayed so they may remain alive a few days.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r13.anchor: والمعنى على ماروى عن أبي مسلم أخر آجالنا وابقنا أياما

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r14.claim: They promise to answer the call to God and His oneness, or the call made through the messengers; the wording implies they now accept the messengers as God’s envoys.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r14.anchor: أي الدعوة اليك والى توحيدك أو دعوتك لنا على ألسنة الرسل عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r15.claim: They promise to make up for having failed to answer the call and follow the messengers; the two clauses reinforce one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r15.anchor: نتدارك مافرطنا به من اجابة الدعوة واتباع الرسل عليهم السلام ولا يخلو ذكر الجملتين عن تأكيد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r16.claim: The plural ‘messengers’ may reflect their shared call to monotheism and the unity of rejecting them, or represent all wrongdoers’ promises across nations to follow each community’s own messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r16.anchor: وجمع اما باعتبار اتفاق الجميع على التوحيد وكون عصيانهم للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عصيانا لهم جميعا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r17.claim: The rebuke is coordinated with ‘they say’ by supplying an implied ‘it is said to them’ before the question.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p247#2/r17.anchor: على تقدير القول معطوفا على فيقول والمعطوف عليه هذه الجملة أي فيقال لهم توبيخا وتبكيتا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r1.claim: The oath may deny any departure from worldly enjoyment, or, through their actions and ambitions, reveal that they expected no transfer to another state and imagined a long delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r1.anchor: مما أنتم عليه من التمتع بالحظوظ الدنياوية أو بألسنة الحال ودلالة الأفعال حيث بنيتم مشيدا وأملتم بعيدا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r2.claim: ‘No departure’ may mean no move from the world to another abode of recompense; Mujāhid relates this to their oath that the dead would not be raised, as in 16:38.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r2.anchor: أو مالكم من زوال وانتقال من دار الدنيا إلى دار أخرى للجزاء كقوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r3.claim: Mujāhid connects their oath with the declaration that God would not raise the dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r3.anchor: وروى هذا عن مجاهد وأياما كان

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r4.claim: On the apparent reading, fa-mā lakum answers their oath, min reinforces the negation, and the second-person address echoes ‘you swore’ to heighten the rebuke rather than saying ‘we.’
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r4.anchor: ( فمالكم ) الخ جواب القسم و ( من ) صلة لتأكيد النفي وصيغة الخطاب فيه لمراعاة حال الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r5.claim: A less apparent reading treats ‘what means have you to depart this state?’ as God’s response to their plea, with the answer to their oath omitted; al-Ālūsī calls this contrary to the immediate sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r5.anchor: وقيل هو ابتداء كلام من قبل الله تعالى جوابا لقولهم : ( ربنا أخرنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī that Hell’s inhabitants make five pleas: God answers the first four, then silences them after the fifth; they are left gasping and groaning without hope.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p248/r6.anchor: ذكر البيهقي عن محمد بن كعب القرظي انه قال : لاهل النار خمس دعوات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r7.claim: Warn means make them fear; yawm is construed as 'by a day.'

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r8.claim: The day the punishment comes is the Resurrection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r9.claim: Those who did wrong committed idolatry.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r10.claim: Their plea means asking to return to worldly life to answer God's call and follow messengers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p359#2/r10.anchor: {ربنا أخرنا} أمهلنا، {إلى أجل قريب} هذا سؤالهم الرد إلى الدنيا، أي: ارجعنا إليها، {نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r1.claim: They swore in worldly life that they would not leave it, denying resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r1.anchor: {أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل} حلفتم في دار الدنيا، {ما لكم من زوال} عنها أي: لا تبعثون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r2.claim: Baghawī links the denial to the oath in al-Naḥl that God would not raise the dead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p360/r2.anchor: وهو قوله تعالى: {وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت}

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r11.claim: The command to warn is addressed to Muhammad; the day is either Resurrection or death, the first day of their punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r11.anchor: يوم القيامة، أو يوم الموت فإنه أول أيام عذابهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r12.claim: The day is the second object of warn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r13.claim: Those who did wrong are the polytheists and deniers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r14.claim: They ask for punishment to be delayed, for return to worldly life until a near term, or for their lives to be extended briefly so they can believe and answer the call.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r14.anchor: أخر العذاب عنا أو ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى حد من الزمان قريب

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r15.claim: Their promise is a response to the command, as in the parallel construction in 63:10.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r15.anchor: { نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل } جواب للأمر ونظيره لولا أخرتنى إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصلحين

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r16.claim: The words are understood as reported speech, and mā lakum is the oath’s response; direct address matches its grammatical form rather than indirect quotation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r16.anchor: { أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال } على إرادة القول و { ما لكم } جواب القسم جاء بلفظ الخطاب على المطابقة دون الحكاية

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r17.claim: They had sworn they would remain in this world, never removed by death, perhaps from arrogance or delusion as suggested by sturdy buildings and distant hopes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r17.anchor: أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزالون بالموت،

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r18.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r18.claim: Another view says they swore they would not move to another abode after death, remaining in the same state through a further stage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:42-44/r18.anchor: وقيل أقسموا أنهم لا ينتقلون إلى دار أخرى وأنهم إذا ماتوا لا يزالون على تلك الحالة إلى حالة أخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r5.claim: Muḥammad is told to warn all people of what befalls them when punishment arrives and the veil is lifted, whether at death or resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r5.anchor: ما يحل بهم { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } وينكشف عنهم الغطاء بالموت أو البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r6.claim: Before death they are not wholly broken; when punishment comes and their pride falls, they ask for a short reprieve so they can make up their neglect.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r6.anchor: ولما كانوا عند إتيان العذاب قبل الموت لا ينكسرون بالكلية , بين أنهم إذ ذاك على غير هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r7.claim: They seek time to answer God's call and follow the messengers; ijābah here means committing to comply with the caller's request.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r7.anchor: أي استدراكا لما فرطنا فيه ؛ والإجابة : القطع على موافقة الداعي بالإرادة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r8.claim: The promise to follow the messengers is expressed with utmost eagerness, but the promised repentance comes too late.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r8.anchor: فيقال لهم : إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر , أولم تكونوا تقولون : إن عرى صبركم لا تنحل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r9.claim: God rebukes them for earlier oaths, made in ignorance, folly, arrogance, or insolence, and reminds them that they had claimed their resolve would not weaken.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r9.anchor: أي جهلا وسفها أو أشرا وبطرا . ولما لم يكن وقت إقسامهم مستغرقا للزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r10.claim: Al-Biqāʿī gives three possible senses of their oath: they would not leave their disbelief for faith, leave this world for the next, or leave their homes; each boasts that the status quo cannot change.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p194/r10.anchor: عما أنتم عليه من الكفران وعدم الإذعان للإيمان , أو من هذه الدار إلى الدار الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p50/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p50/r14.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p50/r14.claim: Qatada says people are warned in worldly life before punishment arrives.
DURR-FULL:v5p50/r14.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب} يقول: أنذرهم في الدنيا من قبل أن يأتيهم العذاب

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the day punishment comes as Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب} قال: يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r2.claim: Mujahid says the wrongdoers ask for a short delay to do deeds in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r2.anchor: {فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب} قال: مدة يعملون فيها من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r3.claim: Mujahid links the rebuke to their earlier oath that God would not resurrect the dead (16:38).
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r3.anchor: {أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل} لقوله: (وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت)

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r4.claim: Mujahid explains “no departure” as moving from worldly life to the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r4.anchor: {ما لكم من زوال} قال: الانتقال من الدنيا إلى الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the phrase as leaving their present condition for the state they request.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ما لكم من زوال} عما أنتم فيه إلى ما تقولون

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase refers to resurrection after death.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r6.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {ما لكم من زوال} قال: بعث بعد الموت

DURR-FULL:v5p52/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says it reached him that Hell’s inhabitants beg for delay to answer the call and follow messengers, then are reminded of their oath.
DURR-FULL:v5p52/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي رضي الله عنه قال: بلغني أن أهل النار ينادون {ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل}

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r4.claim: Muhammad is to warn all people.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r4.anchor: أي خوفهم جميعا يا محمد يوم يأتيهم العذاب

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r5.claim: The day of punishment may mean the Day of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r5.anchor: أي من يوم القيامة أو من يوم موتهم

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r6.claim: Alternatively it may mean the day they die, since death is the first punishment and its agonies begin then.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r6.anchor: فإنه أول أيام عذابهم حيث يعذبون بالسكرات

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r7.claim: The warning primarily addresses unbelievers and secondarily believers, though believers will not be punished.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r7.anchor: وهذا الإنذار للكفرة أصالة وللمؤمنين تبعية وإن لم يكونوا معذبين

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r8.claim: Those who wronged themselves are the people among them who committed shirk and denied the truth.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r8.anchor: فيقول الذين ظلموا منهم بالشرك والتكذيب

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r9.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life and granted respite.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r9.anchor: ربنا أخرنا ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r10.claim: A near term means a short span or limit of time.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r10.anchor: إلى أجل قريب إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r11.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r11.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī suggests an ellipsis: return us to the possessor of a near term, meaning the world, while delaying punishment.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r11.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي لعل في النظم تضمينا

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r12.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r12.claim: Al-Kāshifī paraphrases the plea as postponing punishment, returning them to the world, and giving a short respite.

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r13.claim: They ask to stay alive long enough to believe and answer God’s call to Him and His oneness.
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r13.anchor: وأبقنا مقدار ما نؤمن بك ونجيب دعوتك

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r14.claim: They promise to follow the messengers’ teachings and make up for neglecting the call and messengers.

BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r15.claim: They are reproached: had they not been given time in worldly life and sworn arrogantly that they would never leave it?
BURSEVI:v4p286#3/r15.anchor: على إضمار القول عطفا على فيقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r1.claim: This warning follows the reminder that God is not heedless of wrongdoers: the Prophet should take comfort, persist in calling them, and warn them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون ( إبراهيم : 42 ) ، أي تسل عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r2.claim: Al-nās can mean all people, with disbelievers intended by the next clause about the wrongdoers; alternatively it directly denotes the familiar polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r2.anchor: والناس يعم جميع البشر . والمقصود : الكافرون ، بقرينة قوله : يوم يأتيهم العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r3.claim: The day clause is the second object of warn, which takes a second object by extension because the verb includes the sense of cautioning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r3.anchor: و { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } . منصوب على أنه مفعول ثانن ل { أنذر } ، وهو مضاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the hadith that every prophet warned his people of the Dajjāl as a parallel for this extended use of warn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r4.anchor: كما في الحديث ( ما من نبي إلا أنذر قومه الدجال ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r5.claim: The 'coming' of punishment is a metonymic expression for its occurrence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r5.anchor: وإتيان العذاب مستعمل في معنى وقوعه مجازا مرسلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r6.claim: The punishment may be the afterlife's punishment or the worldly punishment with which the polytheists were threatened.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r6.anchor: والعذاب : عذاب الآخرة ، أو عذاب الدنيا الذي هدد به المشركون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r7.claim: Those who did wrong here are the polytheists.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r8.claim: If the punishment is in the afterlife, they ask to defer judgment and return to worldly life to answer God's call, as in the plea in 23:99–100; the messengers are all who brought God's call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r8.anchor: فالتأخير بمعنى تأخير الحساب ، أي يقول الذين ظلموا : أرجعنا إلى الدنيا لنجيب دعوتك . وهذا كما في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r9.claim: If they speak at the onset of worldly punishment, delay is literal and 'the messengers' is a singular used figuratively for Muḥammad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r9.anchor: وإن حمل على عذاب الدنيا فالمعنى : أن المشركين يقولون ذلك حين يرون ابتداء العذاب فيهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r10.claim: Qarīb means a short span: time is likened to distance, and they ask for only enough time to answer the call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p247#3/r10.anchor: والقريب : القليل الزمن . شبه الزمان بالمسافة ، أي أخرنا مقدار ما نجيب به دعوتك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r1.claim: Because the preceding clause reports their plea, the following words give its answer through an implied 'it is said to them'; reproach rejects the request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r1.anchor: لما ذكر قبل هذه الجملة طلب الذين ظلموا من ربهم تعين أن الكلام الواقع بعدها يتضمن الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r2.claim: The answer turns from direct acceptance or refusal to an interrogative rebuke, which itself entails refusal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r2.anchor: وقد عدل عن الجواب بالإجابة أو الرفض إلى التقرير والتوبيخ لأن ذلك يستلزم رفض ما سألوه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r3.claim: The opening conjunction hints at an omitted clause refusing their plea: 'No! Had you not sworn…'; the refusal is shortened because the reprimanded do not get their wish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r4.claim: Zawāl means moving from a place and here means leaving the graves for the reckoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r4.anchor: والزوال : الانتقال من المكان . وأريد به هنا الزوال من القبور إلى الحساب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r5.claim: The omitted complement of 'departure' is clear from the context; compare the oath that God will not resurrect the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r5.anchor: وحذف متعلق { زوال } لظهور المراد ، قال تعالى : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r6.claim: The second clause explains their oath without an implied quotation; it keeps second-person address rather than switching to 'we have no departure.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r6.anchor: وجملة ما لكم من زوال } بيان لجملة { أقسمتم } . وليست على تقدير قول محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r7.claim: The oath may have been made by all wrongdoers in earthly life, as polytheist generations received the same teachings from predecessors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r7.anchor: وهذا القسم قد يكون صادر من جميع الظالمين حين كانوا في الدنيا لأنهم كانوا يتلقون تعاليم واحدة في الشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r8.claim: Alternatively, most or some members of those peoples swore it, while the others held the same meaning implicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p248/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك صادرا من معظم هذه الأمم أو بعضها ولكن بقيتهم مضمرون لمعنى هذا القسم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p343#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p343#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p343#2/r1.claim: The passage threatens wrongdoers and consoles the wronged; the address ‘do not think’ is to Muhammad, while the prohibition is intended for others who might think this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p343#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية بجملتها فيها وعيد للظالمين، وتسلية للمظلومين، والخطاب بقوله: تحسبن لمحمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r5.claim: ‘The day’ is the Day of Resurrection and is accusative as the object of ‘warn’; it cannot be an adverb because the Resurrection is not a place of warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r5.anchor: المراد ب يوم يوم القيامة ونصبه على أنه مفعول ب أنذر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r6.claim: ‘Then they say’ is in the nominative, coordinated with ‘comes to them.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r6.anchor: وقوله: فيقول رفع عطفا على قوله: يأتيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r7.claim: The phrase implies ‘it will be said to them’; these omitted words are clear from context.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r7.anchor: وقوله: ولم تكونوا إلى آخر الآية، معناه: يقال لهم، فحذف ذلك إيجازا، إذ المعنى يدل عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r8.claim: ‘You have no departure’ is what they had sworn to: they claimed there would be no leaving the earth after death, denying resurrection from the graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r8.anchor: وقوله: ما لكم من زوال هو المقسم عليه نقل المعنى، ومن زوال معناه من الأرض بعد الموت.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r9.claim: This verse echoes the unbelievers’ oath that God would not raise the dead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p345/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية ناظرة إلى ما حكى عنهم في قوله: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r1.claim: When they see punishment, wrongdoers beg for a brief reprieve so they can answer God's call and follow the messengers, like other rejected pleas to return and do good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن قيل الذين ظلموا أنفسهم، عند معاينة العذاب: {ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r2.claim: God rebuts them: before this moment they swore they would not leave their present worldly state and denied resurrection or recompense, so they now taste the result.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r2.anchor: وقال تعالى رادا عليهم في قولهم هذا: {أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r3.claim: Mujāhid and others explain the oath as denying any transfer from this world to the Hereafter, as the deniers swear in 16:38 that God will not resurrect the dead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p516/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: {ما لكم من زوال} أي: ما لكم من انتقال من الدنيا إلى الآخرة

JISHUMI:v5p3892/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r11.claim: Yawm is a direct object governed by 'warn them,' not an adverb: the Prophet was not commanded to warn on that day itself.
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r11.anchor: يوم نصب لأنه مفعول، والعامل فيه: أنذرهم كأنه قال خوفهم عقاب الله يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v5p3892/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r12.claim: Fa-yaqulu is coordinated with 'it comes to them,' not a result clause, so it is nominative.
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r12.anchor: فيقول عطف على قوله: يأتيهم وليس بجواب ولذلك رفع

JISHUMI:v5p3892/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r15.claim: After mentioning the Day of Judgment, the text describes its terror; punishment is delayed to establish proof, not through heedlessness, and wrongdoers cannot escape.
JISHUMI:v5p3892/r15.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر يوم الحساب بين وصفه وأنه أمهلهم لا عن غفلة لكن للحجة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r1.claim: The threatened day is initially identified as the Day of Resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r1.anchor: مفعول ثان لأنذر وهو يوم القيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r2.claim: The wrongdoers ask to be returned to worldly life and given a short reprieve so they can answer the call and follow the messengers they neglected.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r2.anchor: ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r3.claim: Alternatively, the day is their immediate destruction or death amid torment; then they ask that death or punishment be deferred briefly, as in 63:10.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r3.anchor: أو أريد باليوم : يوم هلاكهم بالعذاب العاجل ، أو يوم موتهم معذبين بشدة السكرات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r4.claim: The question about their former oath can be heard as a spoken boast born of arrogance and ignorance, or as an implicit claim conveyed by building lasting homes and harboring distant hopes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r4.anchor: أن يقولوا ذلك بطرا وأشرا ، ولما استولى عليهم من عادة الجهل والسفه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r5.claim: Their oath either asserted that they would remain in this world without death, or denied that they would be moved to another abode, thus denying resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p529/r5.anchor: أقسمتم أنكم باقون في الدنيا لا تزالون بالموت والفناء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r1.claim: The day of punishment is the Day of Resurrection, when wrongdoers ask to return.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r1.anchor: وأنذرهم باليوم الذي يأتيهم فيه العذاب , يعني يوم القيامة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r2.claim: The verse singles out punishment to threaten sinners, though the day also brings reward and encourages the obedient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r2.anchor: وإنما خصه بيوم العذاب وإن كان يوم الثواب أيضا لأن الكلام خرج مخرج التهديد للعاصي وإن تضمن ترغيبا للمطيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r3.claim: After truth becomes plain in the afterlife, wrongdoers seek return to repair past sins; the afterlife accepts no repentance or new duties.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r3.anchor: طلبوا رجوعا إلى الدنيا حين ظهر لهم الحق في الآخرة ليستدركوا فارط ذنوبهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r4.claim: Their earlier oath that they would not depart means no departure from this world to the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r4.anchor: ما لكم من انتقال عن الدنيا إلى الآخرة , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r5.claim: Their earlier oath means they would not depart from the punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p141#3/r5.anchor: ما لكم من زوال عن العذاب , قاله الحسن

MUJAHID:v1p336/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p336/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p336/r1.claim: The Quraysh had sworn that they would not die or pass away.
MUJAHID:v1p336/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ما لكم من زوال ﴾ يعني لا يموتون لقريش

MUQATIL:14:44-46/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r1.claim: The people Muhammad is commanded to warn are Meccan unbelievers; the wrongdoers are Meccan polytheists.
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r1.anchor: يعني كفار مكة، { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } في الآخرة

MUQATIL:14:44-46/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r2.claim: In the Hereafter, the polytheists ask to return to worldly life and be delayed briefly, promising to answer the call to monotheism and follow Muhammad.

MUQATIL:14:44-46/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:44-46/r3.claim: God recalls their former oath that no dead person would be raised, as stated in 16:38.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r1.claim: The threatened day is the Resurrection; alternatively, it is their immediate destruction by torment, or their death amid agony and meeting angels without good news.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r1.anchor: أي يوم القيامة ويوم مفعول ثان لأنذر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r2.claim: Yawm is the second object of warn, not a time adverb, since the warning does not occur on that day.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r2.anchor: ويوم مفعول ثان لأنذر لا ظرف إذ الانذار لا يكون في ذلك اليوم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r3.claim: Those who did wrong are the unbelievers.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r4.claim: They beg to return to worldly life and receive a short reprieve so they can make up for failing to answer God's call and follow the messengers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r4.anchor: أي ردنا إلى الدنيا وامهلنا إلى أمد وحد من الزمان قريب نتدارك ما فرطنا فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r5.claim: The reply recalls their worldly oath that they would not be moved from their state: they denied resurrection, as in 16:38.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r5.anchor: حلفتم في الدنيا انكم إذا متم لا تزالون عن تلك الحالة ولا تنتقلون إلى دار أخرى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r6.claim: This is the answer to their oath; the direct second-person wording replaces their original first-person words, as with the quoted form aqsa mtum.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p234#2/r6.anchor: وما لكم جواب القسم وإنما جاء بلفظ الخطاب كقوله اقسمتم

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people to be warned are the inhabitants of Mecca.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r2.claim: The day the punishment comes is the Day of Resurrection; punishment is emphasized because the passage threatens sinners, although the day also brings reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r2.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة أي خوفهم ذلك اليوم. وإنما خصهم بيوم العذاب وإن كان يوم الثواب، لأن الكلام خرج مخرج التهديد للعاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r3.claim: Those who wronged are the people speaking on that day.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r5.claim: Once the truth appears in the afterlife, they ask to be returned to worldly life for a short time.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r5.anchor: سألوه الرجوع إلى الدنيا حين ظهر الحق في الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r6.claim: They promise to answer God’s call to Islam.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r7.claim: They promise to follow the messengers.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r8.claim: God’s reply recalls their oaths made in worldly life.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r9.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh swore that they would not be resurrected.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r9.anchor: مجاهد: هو قسم قريش أنهم لا يبعثون

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj connects the oath to the statement in 16:38 that they swore forcefully that God would not resurrect the dead.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r10.anchor: ابن جريج: هو ما حكاه عنهم في قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r11.claim: One interpretation of “no departure” is that there is no transition from worldly life to the afterlife, meaning no resurrection or gathering.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r11.anchor: أحدهما ما لكم من انتقال عن الدنيا إلى الآخرة أي لا تبعثون ولا تحشرون وهذا قول مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r12.claim: A second interpretation says “no departure” means no escape from the punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r12.anchor: الثاني { ما لكم من زوال } أي من العذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r13.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r13.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi’s account that Hell’s people make five requests, receiving answers to four before never speaking again: 40:11–12, 32:12–14, this plea, and 35:37 with God’s reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:44/r13.anchor: وذكر البيهقي عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: لأهل النار خمس دعوات يجيبهم الله في أربعة

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the phrase is the second object of warn and identifies the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } مفعول ثان لقوله : { وأنذر } وهو يوم القيامة .

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r2.claim: The definite article in al-ʿadhāb refers to the punishment already described: their eyes fixed and their heads raised.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r2.anchor: الألف واللام في لفظ { العذاب } للمعهود السابق ، يعني : وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r3.claim: Warning means frightening people by mentioning harms.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r3.anchor: الإنذار هو التخويف بذكر المضار ، والمفسرون مجمعون على أن قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r4.claim: The commentators agree that the day when the punishment comes is the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r4.anchor: والمفسرون مجمعون على أن قوله : { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } هو يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r5.claim: Abū Muslim instead places the scene at the moment of death, when the dying person sees what is coming.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r5.anchor: وحمله أبو مسلم على أنه حال المعاينة ، والظاهر يشهد بخلافه

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects Abū Muslim's timing: the request to return and the rebuke about denying departure fit the Resurrection, not death.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r6.anchor: لأنه تعالى وصف اليوم بأن عذابهم يأتي فيه وأنهم يسألون الرجعة ، ويقال لهم :

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r7.claim: Abū Muslim supports his reading by comparing the request for delay with the dying person's plea in the verse about giving charity before death.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r7.anchor: وحجة أبي مسلم : أن هذه الآية شبيهة بقوله تعالى : { وأنفقوا مما * رزقناكم

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r8.claim: One reported view is that the wrongdoers ask to return to worldly life and make up what they neglected.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r8.anchor: فقال بعضهم : طلبوا الرجعة إلى الدنيا ليتلافوا ما فرطوا فيه

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r9.claim: Another view is that they ask to return to a state of religious obligation, as shown by their promise to answer God and follow the messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r9.anchor: وقال : بل طلبوا الرجوع إلى حال التكليف بدليل قولهم : نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r10.claim: Their earlier oath denied moving from this life to another and from this abode to recompense, not ordinary change from life to death, youth to old age, or poverty to wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r10.anchor: ومعنى : ما لكم من زوال ، لا شبهة في أنهم كانوا يقولون لا زوال لنا من هذه الحياة إلى حياة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r11.claim: The rebuke recalls the unbelievers' emphatic oath that God would not resurrect the dead.
RAZI-FULL:v19p112#2/r11.anchor: ومعناه ما ذكره الله تعالى في آية أخرى ، وهو قوله تعالى : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت }

QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r12.claim: The wrongdoers spoiled their earlier affairs and fell short of their obligations; no later repair or excuse can undo this, so the criminal is exposed and judgment falls.
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r12.anchor: أفسدوا في أول أمورهم ، وقصروا في الواجب عليهم ، ولم يكن للخلل في أحوالهم جبران

QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r13.claim: God addresses later hearers: earlier offenders were punished as a lesson, but you imitated them and were deluded by the respite, so expect the recompense for your own deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r13.anchor: وأشهدناكم ذلك مما اعتبرتم ، وجريتم على منهاجهم ، وفعلتم مثل فعلهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r14.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r14.claim: Keeping company with or living near people of passion and sin counts as sharing in their actions, and leads to the same ruin.
QUSHAYRI:v2p129/r14.anchor: ويقال إن معاشرة أهل الهوى والفسق ومجاورتهم مشاركة لهم في فعلهم

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r1.claim: The Day when the punishment comes is the Day of Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r1.anchor: The reference here is to the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r2.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands “mankind” here specifically as the Makkan idolaters.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r2.anchor: According to Ibn ʿAbbās, by mankind is meant the Makkan idolaters specifically

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r3.claim: The wrongdoers request reprieve when punishment makes the truth plain in the Hereafter, echoing their plea to return in 6:27–28 and 32:12; 40:49–50.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r3.anchor: when they see the punishment—that is, when the truth is made manifest to them in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r4.claim: The request is futile: even if returned to earthly life, they would resume what was forbidden and are liars, as 6:28 explains.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r4.anchor: they would return to the very thing they had been forbidden. Truly they are liars

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r5.claim: The end they denied is their passage from worldly life to the Hereafter and its punishment.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r5.anchor: is their going from the life of this world to the Hereafter and the punishment in the Hereafter itself

STUDYQURAN:14:44/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r6.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r6.claim: Many commentators connect this oath denying any end with the Makkan idolaters' oath that God would not resurrect the dead in 16:38.
STUDYQURAN:14:44/r6.anchor: Many commentators connect the last part of this verse

TAB-FULL:v13p714/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r1.claim: Muhammad is to warn those he was sent to call to Islam of what awaits them when God's punishment arrives on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: وأنذر يا محمد الناس الذين أرسلتك إليهم داعيا إلى الإسلام ما هو نازل بهم، يوم يأتيهم عذاب الله في القيامة

TAB-FULL:v13p714/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r2.claim: The wrongdoers are disbelievers who wronged themselves; they ask that punishment be deferred and they be given a short respite to answer the truth's call, believe without associating anything with God, and follow the messengers in obedience.
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r2.anchor: فنؤمن بك، ولا نشرك بك شيئا، {ونتبع الرسل} [إبراهيم: 44] يقولون: ونصدق رسلك فنتبعهم على ما دعوتنا إليه

TAB-FULL:v13p714/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the warned-of day as the Day of Resurrection and explains the requested near term as a period in this world in which they could act.
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قوله: {وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب} [إبراهيم: 44] قال: " يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v13p714/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r4.claim: Qatadah says the warning is to be delivered in this world before the punishment comes.
TAB-FULL:v13p714/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: {وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب} [إبراهيم: 44] يقول: «أنذرهم في الدنيا قبل أن يأتيهم العذاب»

TAB-FULL:v13p715/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r1.claim: The verb “they will say” is nominative, coordinated with “it comes”; it is not the response to the command to warn. If it were that response, either nominative or accusative would be possible, with nominative as a new sentence.
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r1.anchor: وليس بجواب للأمر، ولو كان جوابا لقوله: {وأنذر الناس} [إبراهيم: 44] جاز فيه الرفع والنصب

TAB-FULL:v13p715/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r2.claim: An anonymous poetic line illustrates the accusative construction after the command: “so we may rest,” with the verb after fa in the accusative.
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r2.anchor: يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا … إلى سليمان فنستريحا

TAB-FULL:v13p715/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r3.speaker: العلاء بن سيابة
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r3.claim: Al-Ala ibn Sayyaba rejected the accusative after fa as a response to a command.
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r3.anchor: عن العلاء بن سيابة أنه كان ينكر النصب في جواب الأمر بالفاء

TAB-FULL:v13p715/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r4.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r4.claim: Al-Farra says al-Ala ibn Sayyaba was the one who taught Muadh and his companions.
TAB-FULL:v13p715/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: وكان العلاء هو الذي علم معاذا وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v13p716/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r1.claim: God reproaches Quraysh's disbelievers in Hell for denying resurrection: in worldly life they had sworn they would not move from this world to the next and would not be raised after death.
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r1.anchor: يقول: ما لكم من انتقال من الدنيا إلى الآخرة، وأنكم إنما تموتون، ثم لا تبعثون؟ كما

TAB-FULL:v13p716/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r2.claim: Mujahid links their oath to 16:38 and explains “no departure” as passage from this world to the next.
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قال: {أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل} [إبراهيم: 44] كقوله: {وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت، بلى} [النحل: 38]

TAB-FULL:v13p716/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r3.claim: In another report, Mujahid glosses “no departure” as “you do not die,” addressing Quraysh.
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {ما لكم من زوال} [إبراهيم: 44] قال: «لا تموتون، لقريش»

TAB-FULL:v13p716/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b reports that people in Hell cry for delay so they can obey, and God answers by recalling their earlier oath and the dwellings of earlier wrongdoers (14:45–46).
TAB-FULL:v13p716/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن أبي ليلى أحد بني عامر قال: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي، يقول: " بلغني، أو ذكر لي، أن أهل النار ينادون:

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r1.claim: The warning concerns an exterminating punishment that removes the unjust among a community; as in 10:103, only a group of wrongdoers is struck, not every individual.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r1.anchor: وإنما يصيب الأمة الظالمة بحلول أجلهم وهم طائفة من ظالمي الأمة لا جميع أفرادها

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r2.claim: Extermination is a judgment between a messenger and those who reject the call, prescribed for communities including Muḥammad’s, and repeatedly threatened in the Qur’an.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير سورة يونس وغيره أن ذلك مكتوب على الأمم قضاء بينهم وبين رسولهم

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r3.claim: This day purges the earth of idolatry and injustice until only believers remain and all religion belongs to God; he connects it with the promise that righteous servants inherit the earth.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r3.anchor: وهذا هو اليوم الذي يطهر الله الأرض فيه من قذارة الشرك والظلم

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r4.claim: The claim that the preceding restriction confines punishment to Resurrection does not rule out a different worldly punishment; reading this warning as only Resurrection would override its context and the many verses predicting punishment for this community.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r4.anchor: ولا ينافي انحصاره في يوم القيامة وجود نوع آخر من العذاب في الدنيا

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r5.claim: The wrongdoers are those overtaken by extermination; they ask for a short extension of earthly life to make up what their wrongdoing made them lose, as their promise to answer and follow shows.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r5.anchor: الاستمهال بمدة قصيرة تضاف إلى عمرهم في الدنيا حتى يتداركوا فيه ما فوتوه بظلمهم

TABATABAI:14:42-52/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r6.claim: They say “the messengers” in the plural because the principle behind this punishment is judgment between every messenger and those who reject him, not a rule limited to one messenger.
TABATABAI:14:42-52/r6.anchor: والتعبير بالرسل بلفظ الجمع في قولهم

TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r1.claim: An oath stakes a claim on something honored to establish its truth and is among the strongest means of emphasis; here it may figuratively mean a categorical, unequivocal assertion.
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r1.anchor: الإقسام تعليق الحكم في الكلام بأمر شريف من جهة شرافته

TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r2.claim: The implied speaker rebukes them: they had confidently claimed their power and defenses made them a lasting, dominant community, so why now ask for more time?
TABATABAI:14:42-52#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى يقال لهم توبيخا وتبكيتا ألم تكونوا أقسمتم

FARRA:v2p78#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p78#2/r4.claim: فيقول is nominative with يأتيهم, not a subjunctive answer to the command; an anonymous poem shows a subjunctive answer is possible.
FARRA:v2p78#2/r4.anchor:
رفع تابع ليأتيهم وليس بجواب للأمر ولو كان جوابا لجاز نصبه ورفعه، كما قال الشاعر :
يا ناق سيري عنقا فسيحا ...
إلى سليمان فنستريحا

FARRA:v2p78#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p78#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p78#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s teacher al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Siyyābah rejected subjunctive after fāʾ as an answer to a command; al-Farrāʾ says resumption with fāʾ is good.
FARRA:v2p78#2/r5.anchor: وكان شيخ لنا يقال له: العلاء بن سيابة

THALABI:v5p325/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p325/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p325/r15.claim: The warned-of day is Judgment Day; wrongdoers, meaning disbelievers, ask to be returned to worldly life briefly so they can answer God's call and follow the messengers.
THALABI:v5p325/r15.anchor: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب وهو يوم القيامة فيقول عطف على يوم يأتيهم وليس بجواب

THALABI:v5p325/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p325/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p325/r16.claim: The clause fa-yaqūlu is coordinated with yawm yaʾtīhim, not an answer to the command to warn.
THALABI:v5p325/r16.anchor: فيقول عطف على يوم يأتيهم وليس بجواب فلذلك وقع الذين ظلموا أشركوا ربنا

THALABI:v5p325/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p325/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p325/r17.claim: The near term requested means worldly life: they ask to be returned there to obey God's call and follow the messengers.
THALABI:v5p325/r17.anchor: إلى أجل قريب وهو الدنيا يعني أرجعنا إليها نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل

THALABI:v5p325/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p325/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p325/r18.claim: Their earlier oath that there would be no departure or resurrection echoes the statement that they swore God would not raise the dead.
THALABI:v5p325/r18.anchor: أولم تكونوا أقسمتم حلفتم من قبل في دار الدنيا ما لكم من زوال فيها أي لا يبعثون، وهو قوله وأقسموا بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r3.claim: After completing the description of disbelievers and their resurrection state, the discourse returns to addressing the Prophet with a command to warn, linked to the preceding warning not to think God heedless.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r3.anchor: هذا عطف على قوله: {ولا تحسبن الله غافلا} لأنه قد تم وصف الكفار وحالهم عند البعث في القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people to warn are Mecca's inhabitants; he adds that their following the Prophet would have left no pair in disagreement, and that Walid ibn al-Mughira's faith would have brought everyone along.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني أهل مكة (¬1)، قال: ولو أن أهل مكة اتبعوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ما اختلف عليه اثنان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r5.claim: Yawma is the object of anẓir, as in warn him of punishment; it is not an adverb of time because the Prophet was not commanded to warn on that day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p503/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {يوم يأتيهم العذاب} (يوم) مفعول به، والعامل فيه أنذرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r1.claim: The clause fa-yaqulu is coordinated with yaʾtihim and means that the wrongdoers will speak on that day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فيقول} عطف {يأتيهم}؛ يعني: فيقولون في ذلك اليوم، {الذين ظلموا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses those who did wrong as those who associated partners with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r2.anchor: {الذين ظلموا} قال ابن عباس: يريد أشركوا (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r3.claim: They ask for a short reprieve so they can answer God's call and follow the messengers; Ibn Abbas says they are asking to return to worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p504/r3.anchor: {ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب} استمهلوا مدة يسيرة لكي يجيبوا الدعوة ويتبعوا الرسل، قال ابن عباس: يريدون الرجعة إلى الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r1.claim: Those who did wrong are the polytheists.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r2.claim: They seek a brief delay so they can answer God's call and follow the messengers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r2.anchor: { ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب } استمهلوا مدة يسيرة كي يجيبوا الدعوة، فيقال لهم:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r3.claim: The rebuke recalls their worldly oath that they would not be resurrected or moved to the Hereafter, as another verse says.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:44/r3.anchor: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت...

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r1.claim: Those who reject God's oneness, associate partners with Him, and deny the afterlife and final judgment will regret their worldly conduct at the sight of punishment and seek respite to repair what they missed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r1.anchor: Bu dünyada Allah’ın birliğine inanmayan, O’na ortak koşan, âhiret hayatını ve Allah’ın oradaki nihaî yargılamasını inkâr eden, dolayısıyla kendilerine kötülük eden kimseler âhiret azabını gördüklerinde dünyada yaptıklarına pişman olacaklar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r2.claim: Their plea for a short delay means they want to return to worldly life, believe, and do good works so they can escape the punishment of the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r2.anchor: “Rabbimiz! Bize kısa bir süre daha ver” meâlindeki cümle zalimlerin, iman edip güzel işler yapmak, böylece âhiret azabından kurtulmak için dünyaya geri gönderilmek istediklerini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r3.claim: The question is a rebuke and reproach, showing that the wrongdoers' plea for a delay will not be granted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r3.anchor: “Sizin için bir yok oluş bulunmadığına daha önce yemin etmemiş miydiniz?” meâlindeki soru, kınama ve yerme mahiyetinde olup zalimlerin bu isteklerinin yerine getirilmeyeceğini gösterir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r4.claim: By their earlier oaths, the deniers claimed that there would be no resurrection after death and no punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r4.anchor: İnkârcı zalimler bu yeminleriyle öldükten sonra dirilme olmayacağını ve herhangi bir cezaya çarptırılmayacaklarını iddia ediyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r5.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r5.claim: The wrongdoers knew how calamities had befallen Noah's, ʿĀd's, and Thamūd's peoples because they had settled in and lived around their lands.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r5.anchor: zalimler onların başına gelen felâketlerden haberdardı; çünkü onların yurtlarına yerleşip aynı çevrede yaşamışlardı (Taberî, XIII, 243)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r6.claim: Prophets had also offered comparable examples as lessons: the God who created people from nothing can resurrect them and punish them in the afterlife as He punished them in this world, but they ignored the signs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r6.anchor: insanı yoktan yaratan Allah’ın onu öldükten sonra diriltebileceğine ve dünyada cezalandırdığı gibi âhirette de cezalandırabileceğine işaret edilmişti. Fakat onlar bunu görmezlikten ve işitmezlikten gelmişlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r7.claim: God commands the Prophet to warn people so they do not reach this plight and instead prepare for the afterlife while still in this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:44/r7.anchor: 44. âyette Allah Teâlâ, insanların bu kötü duruma düşmemeleri ve dünyada iken âhiret hayatına hazırlık yapmaları için onları uyarmasını Hz. Peygamber’e emretmiştir

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r1.claim: Pun is valuable through useful meaning despite its surface repetition; Abū al-Fatḥ al-Bustī’s strained examples fail, while better examples make the repeated forms serve an apt thought.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r1.anchor: حسن الإفادة مع ان الصورة صورة التكرير والإعادة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r2.claim: With repeated endings, the listener first expects the old word to recur, then hears a changed word; that delayed realization creates surprise and a sense of gain.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r2.anchor: تتوهم قبل أن يرد عليك آخر الكلمة كالميم من عواصم والباء من قواضب أنها هي التي مضت

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r3.claim: When the words differ from their beginnings, as in al-Buḥturī’s example, a faint expectation of repetition remains, though it is weaker than the effect of shared endings.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p12/r3.anchor: ( بسيوف إيماضها أوجال للأعادي ووقعها آجال )

BURHAN:v4p37/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p37/r6.claim: In ‘we answer Your call and follow the messengers,’ the article in ‘the messengers’ supplies the possessive sense ‘Your messengers.’

DAMGHANI:v1p220/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r2.claim: Zawāl can mean cessation from worldly life; the people deny that they will depart from the world or be resurrected.
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r2.anchor: الزوال الانقطاع قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم
